newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sees important announcements at Lebanon meet.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sees important announcements at Lebanon meet.

text.p: The U.S. State Department said Friday important announcements would be made at an international meeting on aid to Lebanon next week, but would not say if a U.S. ban on travel to Lebanon would be eased.

Some 30 countries and international financial institutions have been invited to the one-day "Friends of Lebanon" conference Monday at the State Department which will discuss reconstruction of the country ravaged by a 16-year civil war.
U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher will lead the U.S. delegation and chair the meeting. The Lebanese delegation will be led by Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri.

"I think you should treat this as a serious event, an event I think the press corps will have a lot of interest in in terms of some of the announcements we'll be making," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
Asked about the travel ban, for whose lifting Beirut has been pressing for years, Burns called it "a very complicated complex issue" but said it had been looked at again this week.

"I don't want to anticipate what decisions may or may not be made on it, but it's certainly an issue that I think Prime Minister Hariri will bring to the table on Monday ... and we'll be prepared to discuss it with him," he added.

Washington insists that its ban on U.S. citizens travelling to Lebanon is a purely security matter dating back to the seizure of American hostages by pro-Iranian groups there in the 1980s. But Beirut suspects it is being used as a lever to force it into signing a peace treaty with Israel.
Lebanon officials in Washington said they did not know if the ban would be lifted but were hopeful of some relaxation.
"There are a lot of indications that the U.S. administration might decide to lift, not all the restrictions, but some of them," said one official who requested anonymity.

George Cody, executive director of American Task Force for Lebanon, a Lebanese-American pressure group, said such a decision would be politically easier for Christopher, who retires next month, than for his successor Madeleine Albright.
Lebanese officials said they expected the United States and other countries to announce aid packages for Lebanon.

Participants at the meeting will include French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette, involved in an alleged U.S.-French diplomatic tiff at a NATO meeting in Brussels this week. U.S. officials said he walked out of a diplomatic toast in honour of Christopher but de Charette's office said he intended no snub.
Burns said Christopher and de Charette were expected to confer on the sidelines of the meeting but no formal bilateral meeting was scheduled.
